# Add v2 updateinfo API endpoint with product slug support

## Summary

This PR introduces a new v2 updateinfo API endpoint that supports product slugs and aggregates advisories across minor versions. It also fixes a critical bug in module package source RPM matching that was causing module packages to be excluded from updateinfo.xml generation.

## Changes

**New v2 API Endpoint:**
- Added `/api/updateinfo/{product}/{major_version}/{repo}/updateinfo.xml` endpoint
- Supports product slugs (e.g., "rocky-linux", "rocky-linux-sig-cloud") instead of exact product names
- Aggregates all advisories for a major version across minor versions
- Requires architecture parameter to prevent cross-architecture package contamination
- Includes data integrity validation to prevent cross-product package contamination

**Bug Fix:**
- Fixed module package source RPM matching bug where packages with "module." prefix were not matching their binary packages
- Module source packages have format "module.package-name" while binary packages use "package-name"
- Now correctly strips "module." prefix during matching to ensure module packages appear in updateinfo.xml

**Code Refactoring:**
- Extracted source RPM mapping logic into reusable `build_source_rpm_mapping()` function
- Created `generate_updateinfo_xml()` function to share XML generation logic between v1 and v2 endpoints
- Added `resolve_product_slug()` for product name resolution

**Testing:**
- Added comprehensive unit tests for product slug resolution
- Tests cover case insensitivity, invalid inputs, and slug format validation

## Technical Details

The v2 endpoint uses explicit `supported_product_id` filtering at multiple levels to ensure data integrity:
- Filters affected_products by supported_product_id
- Double-checks advisory packages match the same supported_product_id
- Logs and skips packages with mismatched product IDs to prevent cross-contamination

This is critical for multi-tenant environments where a single database contains advisories for multiple products.

author: cconlon
body:
# Description

This PR prevents `--enable-all` from enabling QUIC and ECH when `--enable-jni` is also specified, as these are incompatible with `WOLFSSL_TLS13_MIDDLEBOX_COMPAT` mode enabled by JNI. Changes include:

- `configure.ac`: Modified `--enable-all` logic to exclude QUIC and ECH when `$enable_jni = "yes"`
- `tests/api/test_tls13.c`: Skip `test_tls13_hrr_different_cs()` when `WOLFSSL_TLS13_MIDDLEBOX_COMPAT` is defined

Without these changes, `make check` fails with `./configure --enable-jni --enable-all`.

---

**QUIC incompatibility:**
  - TLS 1.3 middlebox compatibility (RFC 8446 Appendix D.4) requires echoing a 32-byte session ID in ClientHello
  - QUIC (RFC 9001 Section 8.4) requires the legacy_session_id field to be empty
  - These requirements seem mutually exclusive

**ECH incompatibility:**
  - ECH (draft-ietf-tls-esni-25) requires `ClientHelloInner.legacy_session_id` to be empty before encryption
  - Middlebox compatibility mode populates session IDs based on client random, violating ECH requirements
  - There might be future work here for compatibility in `GetTls13SessionId()`, but simply skipping this test combo for now.

# Testing

Tested various enable combinations between the above with built-in tests.

# Checklist

 - [ ] added tests
 - [ ] updated/added doxygen
 - [ ] updated appropriate READMEs
 - [ ] Updated manual and documentation

body:
## Fix nullable warning in object initializer member using extension Add method

### Problem
When using implicit extension member access methods (the new `extension` feature) in object initializer collection Add calls, unexpected nullable warnings are reported. The warning incorrectly references the implicit receiver parameter instead of the actual user-provided parameter.

### Root Cause
For implicit extension member access methods in collection initializers:
- The receiver is stored in `ImplicitReceiverOpt`, not in the Arguments array
- The nullable flow analysis wasn't creating a synthetic receiver argument for analysis
- This caused parameter-to-argument mapping to be incorrect, leading to spurious warnings

### Solution
Modified `VisitCollectionElementInitializer` in NullableWalker to:
- Detect implicit extension member access methods (`IsExtensionBlockMember()`)
- Call `ReInferMethodAndVisitArguments` for new extension methods when not delaying completion (reusing existing logic)
- For delayed completion scenarios, manually prepend receiver result after visiting arguments
- Update `addMethodAsMemberOfContainingType` and `setUpdatedSymbolAsContinuation` to handle this case

The fix leverages existing `ReInferMethodAndVisitArguments` logic to avoid duplication and ensure consistent handling of new extension methods.

### Testing
- Added comprehensive test case covering both valid and nullable argument scenarios
- All 4480 nullable reference type tests pass
- All 2052 extension tests pass

## Description

Implements Task 1.4 from the refactoring plan: pure domain models representing encryption state for CCI to CIA conversion. No crypto operations—just data structures with validation and computed properties.

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Test improvement
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [x] Code refactoring
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Related Issues

Related to project-plans/refactoring-plan.md Task 1.4

## Changes Made

**New Models:**
- `EncryptionType` enum: DECRYPTED, ZEROKEY, ORIGINAL_NCCH
- `EncryptionContext` dataclass: encapsulates encryption state with validation

**Implementation:**
```python
from dsconv.models import EncryptionContext, EncryptionType

# Create encryption context
ctx = EncryptionContext(
    encryption_type=EncryptionType.ORIGINAL_NCCH,
    normal_key=derived_key,  # 16 bytes or None
    title_id=title_id_bytes  # 8 bytes
)

# Query encryption state
if ctx.needs_decryption:
    # Handle encrypted content
    pass
```

**Key Features:**
- Validation in `__post_init__`: type checking, byte length verification
- Property methods: `needs_decryption`, `is_decrypted`, `is_zerokey`, `is_original_ncch`
- Zero dependencies on I/O, crypto, or global state
- Follows existing model patterns (dataclass, properties, from_bytes pattern ready)

author: rapidbnnuy
body:
# Pull Request Summary

##  Issues Fixed

### 1. Moderation Double Post
- Fixed an issue where **moderation failures** would post **twice** — once for the failure and once for the rebuke.
- Moderation failure outputs now **respect the “Post To Chat” global variable**, preventing unintended chat messages when disabled.

### 2. Speak and Post-To-Chat Obedience
- Audited all `Speak()` and `CPH.SendMessage()` calls to ensure they **respect global settings**:
  - `Post To Chat`
  - `voice_enabled`
- Fixed cases where chat or TTS output would still occur even when globally disabled.

### 3. CleanAIText Normalization
- Fixed slash (`/`) removal under **HumanFriendly** mode — slashes are now preserved and displayed properly in text like “10/10” or dates.
- Normalized handling of `" - "` (space-hyphen-space) patterns; now replaced with a **single space** for clean, natural flow.
- Adjusted replacement order so the `" - "` cleanup occurs **at the final stage** of text normalization.

---

##  New Feature: Prompt Scorecard & Token Tracking

### Overview
Added a **Prompt Scorecard** that logs per-prompt token usage, cost estimates, and rolling 30-day totals in LiteDB.

### Key Features
- **Per-Prompt Metrics:** Logs model name, prompt tokens, completion tokens, and total tokens.
- **Cost Estimation:** Computes estimated input/output costs using Streamer.bot global variables:
  - `model_input_cost`
  - `model_output_cost`
- **Rolling 30-Day Totals:** Maintains a running 30-day window of token usage (`token_usage` collection).
- **Auto-Cleanup:** Prunes data older than 30 days to avoid DB bloat.
- **Clean Formatting:** Readable, currency-formatted results with sensible rounding (`C4` for prompt cost, `C2` for rolling total).

---

##  Summary
This PR:
- Resolves moderation and chat/TTS obedience inconsistencies,  
- Improves text normalization behavior, and  
- Introduces a **Prompt Scorecard system** with cost and token tracking — giving developers full visibility into GPT performance and usage efficiency.

author: adriansmares
body:
On some systems, shared objects have names such as `/usr/lib/i386-linux-gnu/libc.so.6`, which means that they are ignored by the module loader. This PR proposes that they are taken into account as well.

This fixes memory allocations on newer systems.

author: copilot
body:
Implements a production-readiness verification system that replaces "trust" with "proof" through controlled patch generation, human review gates, and comprehensive runtime validation.

## Core Architecture

```
Detect → Generate Patch → Queue → Human Review → Apply → Certify → Deploy
```

**Key principle**: No guessing, no full rewrites, no unsafe hallucinations. Surgical patches only, deterministic rules, human approval required.

## Modules Added

**Detection & Analysis**
- `placeholders.py` - Scans for TODO/FIXME/NotImplementedError/localhost/dummy credentials
- `prodcheck.py` - Validates environment (DEBUG=false, CORS, HTTPS origins, FORGE_DOMINION_ROOT)
- `rewriters.py` - Identifies localhost URLs for Forge endpoint conversion

**Patch Generation**
- `autofix/generate_patch.py` - Unified diff generation
- `autofix/apply_patch.py` - Safe patch application with dry-run
- `autofix/reviewers.py` - Human-in-the-loop approval queue
- `coder.py` - Dominion-signed patch proposals

**Production Proof**
- `prodsim.py` - Orchestrates: frontend build → placeholder scan → env validation → backend health → CORS check
- Returns non-zero if any criteria fail

**CLI Commands**
- `make prove` - Run production readiness proof
- `make rewrite` - Scan localhost refs (dry-run by default, requires `BCSE_REWRITE_APPLY=true` to modify)
- `make improve` - Disabled by default (AST transforms too invasive)

## Safety Defaults

All destructive operations are disabled or dry-run by default:

```python
# rewrite command scans only
rewrite_localhost_to_forge(paths, dry_run=True)  # default

# improve command no-ops
def improve(paths):
    print("⚠️ BCSE improve disabled by default")
    return 0
```

## CI Integration

Added `.github/workflows/bridge-proof.yml` that fails PRs if:
- Placeholders detected (TODO, FIXME, stubs)
- Environment unsafe (DEBUG=true, CORS_ALLOW_ALL=true)
- Missing HTTPS origins
- Frontend build fails
- No FORGE_DOMINION_ROOT

## Testing

24 unit tests covering:
- Pattern detection accuracy
- Environment validation logic

from difflib import unified_diff

def generate_patch(old: str, new: str, path: str) -> str:
    diff = unified_diff(
        old.splitlines(keepends=True),
        new.splitlines(keepends=True),
        fromfile=f"a/{path}",
        tofile=f"b/{path}",
    )
    return "".join(diff)

import re, pathlib
from typing import List, Tuple

# patterns that force a hard fail in prod check
PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS = [
    r"\bTODO\b", r"\bFIXME\b", r"\bTBD\b",
    r"raise\s+NotImplementedError", r"\bpass\b\s*(#\s*stub)?",
    r"\bmock(ed)?\b", r"\bstub(s)?\b", r"\bplaceholder\b",
    r"changeme", r"default(_|-)password", r"dummy(key|token|secret)",
    r"http://localhost(:\d+)?", r"https?://example\.com",
    r"ENABLE_SAFE_PLACEHOLDER\s*=\s*True",
    r"SAFE_MODE\s*=\s*True",
]

ALLOWLIST_EXT = {".py", ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".json", ".yaml", ".yml", ".toml"}

def scan(root: str = ".") -> List[Tuple[str, int, str]]:
    hits = []
    for path in pathlib.Path(root).rglob("*"):
        if not path.is_file(): continue
        if path.suffix.lower() not in ALLOWLIST_EXT: continue
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
        except Exception:
            continue
        for pat in PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS:
            for m in re.finditer(pat, text):
                line_no = text.count("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
                snippet = text[max(0, m.start()-40):m.end()+40].replace("\n"," ")
                hits.append((str(path), line_no, snippet))
    return hits

author: dj-ccs
body:
Fix two TypeScript compilation errors in communities.ts:

1. TS6133 (line 73): Unused variable 'request'
   - Solution: Prefix with underscore (_request) to indicate intentionally unused
   - The GET / route doesn't need request data, only uses reply

2. TS2345 (line 132): Type incompatibility in route handler
   - Solution: Remove explicit generic type from FastifyRequest
   - Use type assertion on params destructuring instead
   - Pattern: const { communityId } = request.params as { communityId: string }

REASON FOR TS2345:
When using fastify.post() with three parameters (path, options, handler), TypeScript's inference conflicts with explicit generic types on the handler. The type assertion approach maintains type safety while allowing proper inference.

These are standard Fastify typing patterns, not bugs. The fixes maintain full type safety while allowing TypeScript compilation to succeed.

Resolves: TS6133, TS2345 in src/routes/communities.ts

author: rockythorn
body:
# Fix CSAF parser for modular packages and add EUS filtering

## Summary

This PR fixes the CSAF (Common Security Advisory Framework) parser to correctly extract modular package information and adds filtering to exclude EUS (Extended Update Support) products from advisory processing. It also fixes a bug in the CSV merge logic that was preventing advisory updates from being detected.

## Changes

**Modular Package Extraction Fix:**
- Rewrote package extraction to use `product_tree` structure instead of vulnerability product_status
- New `_extract_packages_from_product_tree()` function traverses the product tree to extract NEVRAs directly from product_id fields
- Correctly handles both regular and modular packages by extracting from product_version entries
- Strips modular suffix (::module:stream) from NEVRAs to get clean package identifiers
- Filters out non-RPM artifacts (containers, etc.) using PURL validation

**EUS Product Filtering:**
- Added `_is_eus_product()` function to detect EUS/E4S/AUS/TUS products
- Checks both CPE product field and product name keywords for reliable detection
- Filters EUS products at multiple levels:
  - During affected product extraction
  - During package extraction from product tree
- Skips advisories that only affect EUS products
- Prevents EUS-only packages from contaminating regular release repositories

**CSV Merge Fix:**
- Fixed merge order to prioritize changes.csv over releases.csv
- changes.csv contains the most recent modification timestamps for advisories
- releases.csv contains original publication dates
- Previous order was causing updated advisories to be skipped if they were already in releases.csv

**Web UI Addition:**
- Added admin interface for managing CSAF index timestamp
- Allows administrators to manually adjust the "last indexed" timestamp
- Useful for reprocessing advisories or troubleshooting ingestion issues

## Technical Details

The previous implementation extracted packages from vulnerability.product_status.fixed, which only contained regular packages. Modular packages are stored in the product_tree structure under product_version entries with format "package-nevra::module:stream". The new implementation correctly traverses this structure and extracts both package types.

EUS products are detected using CPE strings (e.g., cpe:/a:redhat:rhel_e4s:9.0) and product name keywords. These products provide extended support for specific minor versions and should not be mixed with regular releases.

body: Some linux users noticed that the latest builds were taking well over 3 hours. The linux arm64 builds were timing out after 6 hours. I ran an agent to come up with this graph: After using `-ftime-report`, gcc was reporting most of the time was spent in `tree PTA`. GCC does not like seem to like +1500 static inline const variable initializations. Since this was done in settings.h it was getting pulled into all files. It would literally grind my machine to a halt. This PR attempts to work around the issue and make it compatible with MSVC, clang, and gcc. author: wransom-tt
body:
### Ticket
N/A

### Problem description
The Pool2D reader kernel has an extra loop which processes dummy data to prevent deadlocking the compute kernel when some cores process less data than others since the compute kernel expects each core to process the same number of kernel positions.  This is unnecessary and could even cause the compute kernel to pack extra positions of junk data at the back of the output tensor causing out of bounds writes.

I believe there is also a race condition in the Pool2D compute kernel where the pre_tilize_cb is pushed without reserving potentially causing conflicts between UNPACK/PACK.

### What's changed
The number of positions processed by each core is now passed as a runtime argument to compute, and the extra loop has been removed from the reader such that each core processes only it's intended data.

In compute the logic is largely unchanged except for reading the new runtime arguments. Additionality it was necessary to add a new check to push the full TILE_HEIGHT * c_tiles number of pages to the pre_tilize_cb to ensure pointers are in the correct place in the event of a non-full last tile. Finally CB sync logic was added to compute to eliminate the race condition.

A MPWI bug has also been fixed to update the `first_row_val` condition based on `use_split_reader`, this previously had no impact as the dummy loop cancelled out the error.

A new grid sample compute kernel has also been implemented to remove the dependency between grid sample an the pool kernel.

### Checklist
In progress

### [`v1.0.1`](https://redirect.github.com/pydata/patsy/releases/tag/v1.0.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pydata/patsy/compare/v1.0.0...v1.0.1)

This is a bug fix release that:

- Removes an inadvertent hard dependency on pytest.

There are no other changes from 1.0.0.

### [`v1.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/pydata/patsy/releases/tag/v1.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pydata/patsy/compare/v0.5.6...v1.0.0)

This is a major release that bumps the version to 1.0.0 to reflect the maturity of the project, and drops support for Python 2.

- Add explicit support for Python 3.13.
- Drop support for Python 2.7, and remove dependency on the `six` module (thanks [@​a-detiste](https://redirect.github.com/a-detiste)).
- Fix compatibility with `numpy >= 2` (thanks [@​natsukium](https://redirect.github.com/natsukium)).
- Update development status to 'mature'.

### [`v0.5.6`](https://redirect.github.com/pydata/patsy/releases/tag/v0.5.6)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/pydata/patsy/compare/v0.5.5...v0.5.6)

This is a minor release pre-empting some upstream deprecations in `numpy` and `pandas`.

- Avoid using deprecated `is_categorical_dtype` from `pandas` at all in pandas >=0.25. (thanks [@​EpigeneMax](https://redirect.github.com/EpigeneMax), [@​lesteve](https://redirect.github.com/lesteve), [@​bashtage](https://redirect.github.com/bashtage))
- Avoid using deprecated `numpy.row_stack` in favor of `numpy.vstack` in preparation from numpy 2.0.  (thanks [@​bashtage](https://redirect.github.com/bashtage))

body:
## Summary
- treat the 0-7 coverage bucket as part of the same calendar day when mapping shift intervals in the calendar view
- update the solver time-range logic so night shifts contribute to the 0-7 bucket on the day they start while keeping next-day carry-over for daytime slots

## Testing
- python - <<'PY'
import json
from api.solver import solve_shift_scheduling
from api.models import ScheduleRequest

TIME_RANGE_ORDER = ["7-9", "9-15", "16-18", "18-21", "21-24", "0-7"]
TIME_RANGE_INTERVALS = {
    "7-9": (7, 9),
    "9-15": (9, 15),
    "16-18": (16, 18),
    "18-21": (18, 21),
    "21-24": (21, 24),
    "0-7": (24, 31),
}

def covers_interval(shift_start, shift_end, interval):
    start, end = interval
    effective_end = min(shift_end, 24)
    if end <= 24:
        return shift_start < end and effective_end > start
    if shift_end <= 24:
        return False
    after_midnight_start = max(shift_start, 24)
        return after_midnight_start < end and shift_end > start

with open('api/input_data.json', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

req = ScheduleRequest(people=data['people'], wishOffs={})
schedule, shortages, status = solve_shift_scheduling(req)
print('status', status)
rows = {label: {day:0 for day in range(1, data['days']+1)} for label in TIME_RANGE_ORDER}
shifts = {s['code']: s for s in data['shifts']}
for assignments in schedule.values():
    if not assignments:
        continue
    for day_idx, code in enumerate(assignments):
        if not code:
            continue
        shift = shifts[code]
        labels = [label for label in TIME_RANGE_ORDER if covers_interval(shift['start'], shift['end'], TIME_RANGE_INTERVALS[label])]
        day = day_idx + 1
        for label in labels:
            rows[label][day] += 1
        if shift['end'] > 24:
            next_day = day + 1
            if next_day <= data['days']:
                after_midnight_start = max(shift['start'], 24) - 24
                after_midnight_end = shift['end'] - 24
                for label in TIME_RANGE_ORDER:
                    start, end = TIME_RANGE_INTERVALS[label]
                    if start >= 24:
                        continue
                    norm_start = start if start < 24 else start - 24
                    norm_end = end if end <= 24 else end - 24
                    if after_midnight_start < norm_end and after_midnight_end > norm_start:
                        rows[label][next_day] += 1
print('Day9 counts:')
for label in TIME_RANGE_ORDER:
    print(label, rows[label][9])
PY

author: copilot
body:
Image IDs were generated from resized images, causing the same original image to receive different IDs when stored with different `image_size` settings. This breaks deduplication and causes unnecessary storage of duplicates.

**Changes**
- Move `_generate_image_id()` call before resize operation in `ImageFileStore.save_image()`
- ID now computed from original image content, ensuring consistency across different resize configurations

**Before:**
```python
# Resize first
if self.image_size is not None:
    pil_image = pil_image.resize((self.image_size, self.image_size), ...)

# Then generate ID from resized image
if image_id is None:
    image_id = self._generate_image_id(pil_image)  # ❌ ID varies with resize settings
```

**After:**
```python
# Generate ID from original first
if image_id is None:
    image_id = self._generate_image_id(pil_image)  # ✓ ID based on original content

# Then resize
if self.image_size is not None:
    pil_image = pil_image.resize((self.image_size, self.image_size), ...)
```

author: rhnzo12
body:
Changed video upload paths to organize content by type:
- Offer videos: 'videos' -> 'creatorlink/videos'
- Retainer deliverables: 'retainer' -> 'creatorlink/retainer'

Changes made:
- client/src/pages/company-offer-create.tsx: Updated folder to 'creatorlink/videos' (2 instances)
- client/src/pages/company-offer-detail.tsx: Updated folder to 'creatorlink/videos' (2 instances)
- client/src/pages/creator-retainer-detail.tsx: Updated folder to 'creatorlink/retainer'

This provides better organization in Cloudinary storage:
- All creator-related content under 'creatorlink/' prefix
- Offer videos and retainer videos in separate folders
- Easier to manage, search, and apply different policies per folder

All uploads are handled via the existing /api/objects/upload endpoint which accepts a 'folder' parameter and passes it to Cloudinary.

author: robertatnineminds
body:
## Summary
This PR implements a complete enterprise feature for managed custom email domains using Resend as the provider, with Temporal workflow orchestration for domain provisioning, DNS verification, and lifecycle management.

## Implementation Details

**Architecture & Design**
- Product package architecture with EE/OSS split (`@product/email-domains` and `@product/email-settings`)
- Temporal workflow orchestration for long-running domain verification processes
- Service layer pattern with `ManagedDomainService` for domain operations
- Signal-based workflow control for manual refresh triggers and deletion

**Backend Components**
- `ManagedDomainService` - Core service for domain CRUD operations with Resend API integration
- `managedEmailDomainWorkflow` - Temporal workflow with automatic 5-minute polling and signal handlers for refresh/delete
- Email domain activities - Provision, verify, activate, and delete domain operations
- `dnsLookup` service - DNS verification using Node.js dns.promises (TXT, MX, CNAME, A records)
- Domain validation utility - RFC-compliant domain validation with comprehensive edge case handling

**Server Actions & API**
- `getManagedEmailDomains()` - List all managed domains for tenant
- `requestManagedEmailDomain(domain)` - Create domain and trigger workflow
- `refreshManagedEmailDomain(domain)` - Signal workflow to re-check verification
- `deleteManagedEmailDomain(domain)` - Remove domain from provider and database
- Workflow client with signal support for running workflows

**Frontend Components**
- `ManagedEmailSettings` - Main settings UI with tabbed interface (inbound/outbound)
- `ManagedDomainList` - Domain list with status badges and action buttons
- `DnsRecordInstructions` - DNS records display with copy-to-clipboard functionality
- Test harness support with `window.__ALGA_MANAGED_EMAIL_OVERRIDES__` for Playwright testing

**Database Changes**
- Migration to add 'deleting' status to email_domains table
- Uses existing `email_domains` and `tenant_email_settings` tables
- Stores provider domain ID, DNS records (JSON), verification status, and failure reasons

**Workflow Integration**
- Updated workflow action registry to use `ManagedDomainService`
- Graceful fallback to mock responses when service unavailable (OSS builds)
- Dynamic import pattern for database connections in activities

**Testing**
- Unit tests for domain validation covering RFC compliance, edge cases, and invalid formats
- Playwright integration tests for end-to-end domain management workflow
- Integration test utilities with internal admin authentication helper

**Configuration**
- Environment variables: `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_DEFAULT_REGION`, `RESEND_BASE_URL`
- Temporal configuration: `TEMPORAL_ADDRESS`, `TEMPORAL_NAMESPACE`, `EMAIL_DOMAIN_TASK_QUEUE`
- Secret provider integration with fallback to environment variables

**UI/UX Improvements**
- Removed feature flag gating from outbound email settings
- Status indicators: verified (green check), pending (amber clock), failed (red warning)
- Re-check DNS and Remove actions based on domain status
- Real-time loading states for async operations

body:
This pull request introduces multi-interface (multi-NIC) configuration support to the RKE2 node initialization workflow and updates documentation accordingly. It also adds backup YAML manifests for two clusters (`j52domain` and `j64domain`), removes a legacy PowerShell VM provisioning script, and deletes an outdated VM clone CSV. The most significant changes are grouped below.

**Multi-interface networking support and documentation:**

* Added support for defining multiple network interfaces via YAML (`spec.interfaces`), CLI (`--interface` flag), or interactive prompts. The primary interface seeds legacy scalar fields for backward compatibility, and all interfaces are rendered in the final netplan configuration. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R38) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R166-R179) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L216-R236) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R256-R277)

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R195) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5R256-R277)

**Cluster backup manifest additions:**

* Added backup YAML manifests for all nodes (servers, add-servers, and agents) in the `j52domain` and `j64domain` clusters, capturing their network, CA, and cluster configuration for disaster recovery or migration. body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [urllib3](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3) ([changelog](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/main/CHANGES.rst)) | `==1.26.20` → `==2.7.0` | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/pypi/urllib3/2.7.0?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/pypi/urllib3/1.26.20/2.7.0?slim=true) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>urllib3/urllib3 (urllib3)</summary>

### [`v2.7.0`](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.rst#270-2026-05-07)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3/compare/2.6.3...2.7.0)

\=======================

## Security

Addressed high-severity security issues.
Impact was limited to specific use cases detailed in the accompanying
advisories; overall user exposure was estimated to be marginal.

- Decompression-bomb safeguards of the streaming API were bypassed:

  1. When `HTTPResponse.drain_conn()` was called after the response had been
     read and decompressed partially.
  2. During the second `HTTPResponse.read(amt=N)` or
     `HTTPResponse.stream(amt=N)` call when the response was decompressed
     using the official `Brotli <https://pypi.org/project/brotli/>`\_\_ library.

  See `GHSA-mf9v-mfxr-j63j <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-mf9v-mfxr-j63j>`\_\_
  for details.

- HTTP pools created using `ProxyManager.connection_from_url` did not strip
  sensitive headers specified in `Retry.remove_headers_on_redirect` when
  redirecting to a different host.
  (`GHSA-qccp-gfcp-xxvc <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-qccp-gfcp-xxvc>`\_\_)

## Deprecations and Removals

- Used `FutureWarning` instead of `DeprecationWarning` for better
  visibility of existing deprecation notices. Rescheduled the removal of
  deprecated features to version 3.0.
  (`#​3763 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3763>`\_\_)
- Removed support for end-of-life Python 3.9.
  (`#​3720 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3720>`\_\_)
- Removed support for end-of-life PyPy3.10.
  (`#​4979 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/4979>`\_\_)
- Bumped the minimum supported pyOpenSSL version to 19.0.0.
  (`#​3777 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3777>`\_\_)

## Bugfixes

- Fixed a bug where `HTTPResponse.read(amt=None)` was ignoring decompressed
  data buffered from previous partial reads.
  (`#​3636 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3636>`\_\_)
- Fixed a bug where `HTTPResponse.read()` could cache only part of the
  response after a partial read when `cache_content=True`.
  (`#​4967 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/4967>`\_\_)
- Fixed `HTTPResponse.stream()` and `HTTPResponse.read_chunked()` to handle
  `amt=0`.
  (`#​3793 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3793>`\_\_)
- Updated `_TYPE_BODY` type alias to include missing `Iterable[str]`,
  matching the documented and runtime behavior of chunked request bodies.
  (`#​3798 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3798>`\_\_)
- Fixed `LocationParseError` when paths resembling schemeless URIs were
  passed to `HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen()`.
  (`#​3352 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3352>`\_\_)
- Fixed `BaseHTTPResponse.readinto()` type annotation to accept
  `memoryview` in addition to `bytearray`, matching the
  `io.RawIOBase.readinto` contract and enabling use with
  `io.BufferedReader` without type errors.
  (`#​3764 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3764>`\_\_)

### [`v2.6.3`](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.rst#263-2026-01-07)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3/compare/2.6.2...2.6.3)

\==================

- Fixed a high-severity security issue where decompression-bomb safeguards of
  the streaming API were bypassed when HTTP redirects were followed.
  (`GHSA-38jv-5279-wg99 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-38jv-5279-wg99>`\_\_)
- Started treating `Retry-After` times greater than 6 hours as 6 hours by
  default. (`#​3743 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3743>`\_\_)
- Fixed `urllib3.connection.VerifiedHTTPSConnection` on Emscripten.
  (`#​3752 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3752>`\_\_)

### [`v2.6.2`](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.rst#262-2025-12-11)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3/compare/2.6.1...2.6.2)

\==================

- Fixed `HTTPResponse.read_chunked()` to properly handle leftover data in
  the decoder's buffer when reading compressed chunked responses.
  (`#​3734 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3734>`\_\_)

### [`v2.6.1`](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.rst#261-2025-12-08)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3/compare/2.6.0...2.6.1)

\==================

- Restore previously removed `HTTPResponse.getheaders()` and
  `HTTPResponse.getheader()` methods.
  (`#​3731 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3731>`\_\_)

### [`v2.6.0`](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3/blob/HEAD/CHANGES.rst#260-2025-12-05)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/urllib3/urllib3/compare/2.5.0...2.6.0)

\==================

## Security

- Fixed a security issue where streaming API could improperly handle highly
  compressed HTTP content ("decompression bombs") leading to excessive resource
  consumption even when a small amount of data was requested. Reading small
  chunks of compressed data is safer and much more efficient now.
  (`GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37>`\_\_)
- Fixed a security issue where an attacker could compose an HTTP response with
  virtually unlimited links in the `Content-Encoding` header, potentially
  leading to a denial of service (DoS) attack by exhausting system resources
  during decoding. The number of allowed chained encodings is now limited to 5.
  (`GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/security/advisories/GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53>`\_\_)

.. caution::

- If urllib3 is not installed with the optional `urllib3[brotli]` extra, but
  your environment contains a Brotli/brotlicffi/brotlipy package anyway, make
  sure to upgrade it to at least Brotli 1.2.0 or brotlicffi 1.2.0.0 to
  benefit from the security fixes and avoid warnings. Prefer using
  `urllib3[brotli]` to install a compatible Brotli package automatically.

- If you use custom decompressors, please make sure to update them to
  respect the changed API of `urllib3.response.ContentDecoder`.

## Features

- Enabled retrieval, deletion, and membership testing in `HTTPHeaderDict` using bytes keys. (`#​3653 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3653>`\_\_)
- Added host and port information to string representations of `HTTPConnection`. (`#​3666 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3666>`\_\_)
- Added support for Python 3.14 free-threading builds explicitly. (`#​3696 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3696>`\_\_)

## Removals

- Removed the `HTTPResponse.getheaders()` method in favor of `HTTPResponse.headers`.
  Removed the `HTTPResponse.getheader(name, default)` method in favor of `HTTPResponse.headers.get(name, default)`. (`#​3622 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3622>`\_\_)

## Bugfixes

- Fixed redirect handling in `urllib3.PoolManager` when an integer is passed
  for the retries parameter. (`#​3649 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3649>`\_\_)
- Fixed `HTTPConnectionPool` when used in Emscripten with no explicit port. (`#​3664 <https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3/issues/3664>`\_\_)
- Fixed handling of `SSLKEYLOGFILE` with expandable variables

This commit implements a production-ready data collection infrastructure for cryptocurrency futures trading analysis.

## Project Structure
- Organized module structure (data_collector/, data_quality/, schemas/, scripts/)
- Python packages with proper initialization

## Core Components

### Data Collection Modules
- **binance_client.py**: Robust Binance Futures API client
  - Automatic retry logic and rate limiting
  - Support for OHLCV, OI, funding rates, liquidations, long/short ratios

- **historical_collector.py**: Batch historical data collection
  - Smart pagination for large date ranges

author: mohammadfawaz
body:
This PR changes how program imports work when they are available as actual Leo programs. Previously, such imports would be complied separately then decompiled as stubs. Now, they are compiled with the primary program simultaneously. The goal is for programs to be able to share high level features that are not present in Aleo assembly such as option types, non-mapping storage types, const generics, etc. That being said, those things aren't supported just yet. This PR simply aims at changing how imports work without introducing new features.

The changes in this PR are fairly simple but it did take a while to get everything working correctly because a lot of features and compiler internals relied on the fact that all dependencies are stubs generated from Aleo programs.

Things to note:
1. A stub can now be a `FromLeo(Program)` or a `FromAleo(AleoProgram)`.
2. Stubs are still flattened in the top level program like before. It is assumed that they are fed by the package manager in correct dependency order.
3. The symbol table now tracks dependencies using an `imports` map which maps programs to the names of the programs they import.
4. `lookup_*` methods for `SymbolTable` now consule the `imports` map before trying to return an item.
5. External structs are now supported using the locator syntax `external_program.aleo/ExternalStruct`. They work as one might expect.
6. Codegen now produces bytecode for the primary program and its dependencies.

Closes #28839

author: fw-bot
body:
Description
-----------
Avoid self-join of `account_bank_statement` that is done with a `Nested Loop` due to the `LATERAL`. Even if correlated, it requires two separate accesses to its index.
Replaces it with a window function + `LAG` partitioned by the `journal_id`.
This leads to a simpler plan (lower cost) and working in-memory instead of accessing disk pages (lower IO contention).

Benchmark
---------
On a database with 46k `account_bank_statement`, calling `_get_invalid_statement_ids` for all statements took:

| [Before](https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/7605a4ddc42afbcf) | [After](https://explain.dalibo.com/plan/88d6ac1gee37aha3) | Speed-up |
|--------|-------|----------|
| 146ms  | 72ms  | 2x       |

author: livitup
body:
## Summary
Implements ticket #93 - Phase 1 of the Zone Architecture Refactor.

Creates the CodeplugZone join table model to associate zones with codeplugs with position-based ordering.

## Epic
Part of #91 - Zone Architecture Refactor (Phase 1: Foundation)

## Changes

### New Model

**CodeplugZone**
- Join table linking codeplugs to zones
- Associations:
  - `belongs_to :codeplug`
  - `belongs_to :zone`
- Validations:
  - Presence of codeplug, zone, position
  - Position must be > 0
  - Uniqueness of zone within codeplug
  - Uniqueness of position within codeplug
- Default scope: ordered by position (ascending)
- Database indexes:
  - Unique on [codeplug_id, zone_id]
  - Unique on [codeplug_id, position]

### Model Updates

**Codeplug**
- Added `has_many :codeplug_zones, dependent: :destroy`

**Zone**
- Added `has_many :codeplug_zones, dependent: :destroy`
- Added `has_many :codeplugs, through: :codeplug_zones`

## Database Migration

- `20251108032416_create_codeplug_zones.rb`
  - Creates codeplug_zones table with codeplug_id, zone_id, position
  - Adds unique indexes on [codeplug_id, zone_id] and [codeplug_id, position]

## Tests

### New Test File
- `test/models/codeplug_zone_test.rb` - 21 tests covering:
  - Basic validations (presence, associations)
  - Position validation (> 0, uniqueness per codeplug)
  - Zone uniqueness per codeplug
  - Default scope (ordering by position)
  - Through associations (codeplug.zones, zone.codeplugs)

### Test Results
```
21 new tests, all passing
474 total tests: 0 failures, 0 errors, 3 skips
```

### Code Quality
- ✅ Rubocop: 126 files inspected, no offenses detected
- ✅ Brakeman: No security warnings (Models: 18, no issues)

## TDD Workflow

This ticket strictly followed TDD principles:

1. **RED** - Wrote 21 failing tests first
2. **GREEN** - Created migration, model, validations, and factory
3. **VERIFY** - All tests pass, code quality checks pass

## Migration Strategy

Per Epic #91, **Phase 1 tickets can merge to main independently** as they introduce no breaking changes.

## Files Changed

**New Files (4):**
- app/models/codeplug_zone.rb
- db/migrate/20251108032416_create_codeplug_zones.rb
- test/models/codeplug_zone_test.rb
- test/factories/codeplug_zones.rb

**Modified Files (3):**
- app/models/codeplug.rb (added association)
- app/models/zone.rb (added associations)
- db/schema.rb (migrations)

## Next Steps

After merge:
- ✅ Phase 1: 2 of 3 tickets complete (#92 ✅, #93 ✅)
- ⏭️ Next: #94 - Refactor Zone model to be standalone

- [x] Understand current implementation and table rendering logic

## Summary
Refactored the audit log table to move verbose key-value details from inline rendering to hidden DOM nodes. The table now only shows concise chips (HTTP method, path, requestId) in the Details column, with verbose details revealed only when the user clicks the "Details" button to open a modal.

## Changes Made
- Updated `assets/js/audit-ui.js` to create hidden `<pre>` elements with unique IDs (`audit-{index}-pretty` and `audit-{index}-raw`)
- Removed inline verbose key-value preview from the Details column (eliminated ~50 lines of preview rendering code)
- Modified the "Details" button to use `data-base` attribute instead of `data-idx`
- Updated modal handler to find and display content from hidden DOM nodes by ID
- Kept chips (HTTP method, path, requestId) visible in the table for quick scanning
- All linting issues resolved automatically

## Visual Changes
**Before**: Each row showed verbose key-value pairs inline (e.g., "role: admin, rememberMe: false, twoFactorUsed: false..."), making the table cluttered and hard to scan.

**After**: Only concise chips are shown inline. Verbose details are hidden and only displayed when clicking "Details". This makes the table much cleaner and easier to navigate.

## Fix Diagnostic Page Access Issue ✓ COMPLETE

The diagnostic pages were showing "Sorry, you are not allowed to access this page" because they were trying to register as submenus of `wp-mcp-ai-dashboard` which may not exist.

### Changes Made:
- [x] Understand the current issue: diagnostic pages registered under non-existent parent menu
- [x] Fix diagnostic page registration to use Tools menu instead of wp-mcp-ai-dashboard
  - Updated `class-wp-mcp-ai-dashboard-diagnostic.php` to register under `tools.php`
  - Updated `class-wp-mcp-ai-mcp-server-diagnostic.php` to register under `tools.php`
  - Updated `class-wp-mcp-ai-provider-diagnostics.php` to register under `tools.php`
  - Added explanatory comments for why the change was needed
  - Updated menu labels to be more descriptive with "WP oOS" prefix
- [x] Add plugin action links in the Plugins page
  - Added "Settings" link that points to the appropriate settings page (old or new dashboard)
  - Added "Diagnostic" link that points to the diagnostic page under Tools menu
  - Links are displayed in the plugin row in wp-admin/plugins.php
- [x] All changes committed and pushed

### Technical Details:
The diagnostic pages were originally registered as submenus of the `wp-mcp-ai-dashboard` parent menu. However, this parent menu only exists when `WP_MCP_AI_USE_OLD_SETTINGS` is false AND the dashboard initialization succeeds. When the parent menu doesn't exist, WordPress returns the "Sorry, you are not allowed to access this page" error when trying to access non-existent menu pages.

The fix moves all three diagnostic pages to the WordPress Tools menu (`tools.php`), which always exists, ensuring they are accessible regardless of the main dashboard state. This aligns with the comment in `wp-mcp-ai.php` line 278 which already stated these should be "always available under Tools menu".

Additionally, plugin action links were added to make it easier to access the Settings and Diagnostic pages directly from the Plugins page in WordPress admin.

### How to Access Diagnostic Pages:
1. **Via Tools Menu**: Tools → WP oOS Diagnostic / WP oOS MCP Test / WP oOS Provider Test
2. **Via Plugin Links**: Plugins page → WP Open Operator System → Diagnostic link
3. **Direct URL**: `/wp-admin/admin.php?page=wp-mcp-ai-diagnostic`

### Files Modified (4 files, 48 additions, 9 deletions):
- `includes/admin/class-wp-mcp-ai-dashboard-diagnostic.php`
- `includes/admin/class-wp-mcp-ai-mcp-server-diagnostic.php`
- `includes/admin/class-wp-mcp-ai-provider-diagnostics.php`
- `wp-mcp-ai.php`

body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **5.3** to **7.11.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.11.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: if the measurement core defaults to "sysmon" (the default for Python
  3.14+ since v7.9.1), but sysmon can't support some aspect of your
  configuration (concurrency settings, dynamic contexts, and so on), then the
  ctrace core is used instead. Previously, this would result in an error.
  Now a warning is issued instead, explaining the fallback. An explicit request
  for sysmon with conflicting settings will still result in an error. Closes
  `issue 2064`_.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

.. _issue 1420: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1420
.. _issue 2064: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2064
.. _issue 2070: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2070


.. _changes_7-11-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.9, declared support for Python 3.15 alpha.


.. _changes_7-10-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.7
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Performance: with branch coverage in large files, generating HTML, JSON, or
  LCOV reports could take far too long due to some quadratic behavior when
  creating the function and class index pages.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 2048`_.  Thanks to Daniel Diniz for help diagnosing the problem.

- Most warnings and a few errors now have links to a page in the docs
  explaining the specific message.  Closes `issue 1921`_.

.. _issue 1921: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1921
.. _issue 2048: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2048


.. _changes_7-10-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.6
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: ``source`` directories were not properly communicated to subprocesses
  that ran in different directories, as reported in `issue 1499`_.  This is now
  fixed.

- Performance: `Alex Gaynor continues fine-tuning <pull 2038_>`_ the speed of
  combination, especially with many contexts.

.. _issue 1499: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1499
.. _pull 2038: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2038


.. _changes_7-10-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.5
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Big speed improvements for ``coverage combine``: it's now about twice as
  fast! Huge thanks to Alex Gaynor for pull requests `2032 <pull 2032_>`_,
  `2033 <pull 2033_>`_, and `2034 <pull 2034_>`_.

.. _pull 2032: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2032
.. _pull 2033: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2033
.. _pull 2034: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2034


.. _changes_7-10-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.4
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Added ``patch = fork`` for times when the built-in forking support is
  insufficient.

- Fix: ``patch = execv`` also inherits the entire coverage configuration now.


.. _changes_7-10-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fixes for ``patch = subprocess``:

  - If subprocesses spawned yet more subprocesses simultaneously, some coverage
    could be missed.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 2024`_.

  - If subprocesses were created in other directories, their data files were
    stranded there and not combined into the totals, as described in `issue
    2025`_.  This is now fixed.

  - On Windows (or maybe only some Windows?) the patch would fail with a
    ``ModuleNotFound`` error trying to import coverage.  This is now fixed,
    closing `issue 2022`_.

  - Originally only options set in the coverage configuration file would apply
    to subprocesses.  Options set on the ``coverage run`` command line (such as
    ``--branch``) wouldn't be communicated to the subprocesses.  This could
    lead to combining failures, as described in `issue 2021`_. Now the entire
    configuration is used in subprocesses, regardless of its origin.

  - Added ``debug=patch`` to help diagnose problems.

- Fix: really close all SQLite databases, even in-memory ones. Closes `issue
  2017`_.

.. _issue 2017: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2017
.. _issue 2021: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2021
.. _issue 2022: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2022
.. _issue 2024: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2024
.. _issue 2025: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2025


.. _changes_7-10-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some code with NOP bytecodes could report missing branches that are
  actually executed. This is now fixed, closing `issue 1999`_. Python 3.9
  still shows the problem.

.. _issue 1999: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1999


.. _changes_7-10-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the exclusion for ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` was wrong: it marked the branch
  as partial, but it should have been a line exclusion so the entire clause
  would be excluded. Improves `issue 831`_.

- Fix: changed where .pth files are written for ``patch = subprocess``, closing
  `issue 2006`_.

.. _issue 2006: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2006


.. _changes_7-10-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- A new configuration option: ":ref:`config_run_patch`" specifies named patches
  to work around some limitations in coverage measurement.  These patches are
  available:

  - ``patch = _exit`` lets coverage save its data even when :func:`os._exit()
    <python:os._exit>` is used to abruptly end the process.  This closes
    long-standing `issue 310`_ as well as its duplicates: `issue 312`_, `issue
    1673`_, `issue 1845`_, and `issue 1941`_.

  - ``patch = subprocess`` measures coverage in Python subprocesses created
    with :mod:`subprocess`, :func:`os.system`, or one of the :func:`execv
    <python:os.execl>` or :func:`spawnv <python:os.spawnl>` family of
    functions. Closes old `issue 367`_, its duplicate `issue 378`_ and old
    `issue 689`_.

  - ``patch = execv`` adjusts the :func:`execv <python:os.execl>` family of
    functions to save coverage data before ending the current program and
    starting the next. Not available on Windows. Closes `issue 43`_ after 15
    years!

- The HTML report now dimly colors subsequent lines in multi-line statements.
  They used to have no color.  This gives a better indication of the amount of
  code missing in the report.  Closes `issue 1308`_.

- Two new exclusion patterns are part of the defaults: ``...`` is automatically
  excluded as a line and ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` is excluded as a branch.  Closes
  `issue 831`_.

- A new command-line option: ``--save-signal=USR1`` specifies a signal that
  coverage.py will listen for.  When the signal is sent, the coverage data will
  be saved.  This makes it possible to save data from within long-running
  processes.  Thanks, `Arkady Gilinsky <pull 199

body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a bug in `EnhancedNodeInfo.from_dict()` where the method would fail with a `TypeError` when the input dictionary contained keys that aren't valid parameters for the dataclass constructor.

## Changes

- Added parameter filtering in `from_dict()` method using `inspect.signature()`
- Only passes valid dataclass parameters to the constructor
- Filters out any extraneous keys that might be present in the input dict

## Problem Solved

Before this fix, calling `EnhancedNodeInfo.from_dict(data)` would raise a `TypeError` if `data` contained any keys not defined as dataclass fields. This commonly happened when deserializing from external sources or APIs that include additional metadata.

## Implementation Details

- Uses `inspect.signature()` to dynamically get valid parameter names
- Filters the input dictionary to only include recognized parameters
- Maintains backward compatibility - all existing valid calls continue to work
- Improves robustness when working with external data sources

## Test Plan

- Verified existing functionality still works
- Tested with dictionaries containing extra keys
- Confirmed no regression in normal operation

Enables WeLT to operate with only an image encoder by making `bytes_encoder` optional, mirroring existing `image_encoder` optional support.

## Changes

- **welt/config.py**: Fixed `init_sub_config` to use `NoopConfig()` for optional encoders (image_encoder, bytes_encoder) when `None`, ensuring proper serialization during save/load cycles

- **welt/model.py**: Fixed dtype resolution in `encode_images` and `encode_texts` - replaced `getattr(self.encoder, "dtype", fallback)` with explicit conditional to avoid AttributeError when encoder is `None`

- **tests/test_model.py**: Added `test_model_from_pretrained_works_without_bytes_encoder` to verify save/load functionality

## Usage

```python
# Now supported: model with only image encoder
model, processor, collator = setup_model(
    image_encoder_name="WinKawaks/vit-tiny-patch16-224",
    bytes_encoder_name=None,  # Previously would fail on save/load
    latent_transformer_name="EleutherAI/pythia-70m",
    bytes_decoder_name="EleutherAI/pythia-70m"
)

# Save and load works correctly
model.save_pretrained(temp_dir)
loaded = WordLatentTransformer.from_pretrained(temp_dir)
```

**Constraint**: At least one encoder (image or bytes) must be provided.

## Changes provided by this PR

This PR fixes the warning **[W1035] Attribute common.tier is missing in io-package.json** reported by the ioBroker repository checker.

### Background

The `common.tier` attribute in `io-package.json` defines the start order of adapter instances. Allowed values are 1, 2, or 3:

- **Tier 1**: Start first - for critical adapters like database servers that must be started before all other adapters
- **Tier 2**: Start second - for most adapters (default)
- **Tier 3**: Start last - for visualization adapters that should be started after all other adapters

Setting this attribute ensures that adapter instances are started in the correct order during system initialization, which is important for adapters that depend on other adapters being available.

More information about io-package.json attributes can be found in the [ioBroker documentation](https://github.com/iobroker-community-adapters/ioBroker.harmony/issues).

### Changes

This PR adds the `common.tier` attribute to `io-package.json` with the appropriate default value based on the adapter type:
- Visualization adapters (`visualization`, `visualization-icons`, `visualization-widgets`) receive tier 3
- All other adapters receive tier 2

The attribute is placed after `loglevel` if it exists, or before `license`/`licenseInformation` otherwise, following the standard io-package.json structure.

author: erauner12
body:
## Summary

Add support for Auth0-issued RS256 JWT tokens alongside existing HS256 tokens to enable production authentication.

## Problem

The server currently only accepts HS256 (HMAC) tokens with a shared secret, but Auth0 issues RS256 (RSA) tokens that are validated against Auth0's public keys (JWKS).

## Solution

Enhanced the JWT middleware to support both signing methods:
- **RS256 (Auth0)**: Validates tokens using Auth0's JWKS endpoint
- **HS256 (dev/testing)**: Validates tokens using shared secret (existing behavior)
- **X-Debug-Sub (dev mode)**: Bypasses JWT validation when `DevMode=true` (existing behavior)

## Changes

### `internal/auth/jwt.go`
- Added JWKS caching mechanism for Auth0 public keys
- Enhanced `JWTCfg` struct with `Auth0Domain` and `Auth0Audience` fields
- Updated middleware to support both RS256 and HS256 signing methods
- Added issuer and audience claim validation for Auth0 tokens
- Public keys are cached for 1 hour and automatically refreshed

### `cmd/server/main.go`
- Added `AUTH0_DOMAIN` and `AUTH0_AUDIENCE` environment variables
- Updated security validation to allow either Auth0 or HS256 configuration
- Added logging for authentication mode on startup

### `chart/templates/configmap.yaml` & `chart/templates/deployment.yaml`
- Added optional Auth0 configuration to Helm chart
- Auth0 config only applied when `api.auth0` values are set
- Maintains backward compatibility with existing deployments

## Testing

Auth0 API has been provisioned via Terraform with:
- Audience: `https://toolbridgeapi.erauner.dev`
- Scopes: `sync:read`, `sync:write`
- Client grants for all ToolBridge clients (web, iOS/Android, macOS)

Helm values updated in homelab-k8s to configure:
```yaml
api:
  env: production
  auth0:
    domain: "dev-zysv6k3xo7pkwmcb.us.auth0.com"
    audience: "https://toolbridgeapi.erauner.dev"
```

## Dependencies

- Requires: erauner/homelab-k8s@1609f1da (Auth0 Terraform + Helm values)

## Backward Compatibility

✅ Fully backward compatible:
- HS256 tokens still work for dev/testing
- X-Debug-Sub header still works when `DevMode=true`
- Deployments without Auth0 config continue to use HS256

body:
Addressed 9 code review findings across CI/CD workflows and helper scripts covering security vulnerabilities, incorrect error handling, and code clarity issues.

## Security

**gemini-helper.sh** - API key exposure
- Moved API key from URL query string to `x-goog-api-key` header
- Added `jq` for proper JSON escaping to prevent injection attacks

```bash
# Before: API key exposed in URL and prone to injection
curl "...?key=$GEMINI_API_KEY" -d "{\"text\":\"$prompt\"}"

# After: API key in header with safe JSON encoding
json_payload=$(jq -n --arg prompt "$prompt" '{"contents":[{"parts":[{"text":$prompt}]}]}')
curl -H "x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY" -d "$json_payload"
```

## Correctness

**self-healing.yml** - Git diff check missed staged changes
- Changed `git diff --quiet` to `git diff --quiet HEAD` across 3 instances

**release.yml** - Invalid Date construction from SHA
- Fixed by fetching commit object first: `github.rest.git.getCommit()` then using `commitData.data.committer.date`

**deploy.yml** - Incorrect GitHub Actions expression syntax
- Simplified `if: ${{ !github.event.inputs.skip_tests }}` to `if: github.event.inputs.skip_tests != 'true'`

## Code Quality

**self-healing.yml** - Error suppression hiding failures
- Replaced `git commit ... || echo "Nothing to commit"` with `continue-on-error: true` and separate push step

**gemini-helper.sh** - Command substitution without quotes
- Split declaration and assignment: `local var; var=$(command)` for 4 instances

**ci.yml** - Unclear fallback logic in build check
- Replaced chained `||` with explicit `if/elif/else` and explanatory comments

**CI-CD-SETUP.md** - Vague pricing information

author: robobun
body:
## Summary

Adds support for `fs.mkdtempDisposable()` in `node:fs/promises` and `fs.mkdtempDisposableSync()` in `node:fs`.

These functions create temporary directories that automatically clean themselves up when disposed using the `await using` and `using` keywords respectively.

### Implementation details

- **mkdtempDisposable()**: Returns a promise that resolves to a disposable object with:
  - `path`: The created temporary directory path
  - `remove()`: Async function to manually remove the directory
  - `[Symbol.asyncDispose]()`: Automatic cleanup for `await using`

- **mkdtempDisposableSync()**: Returns a disposable object with:
  - `path`: The created temporary directory path
  - `remove()`: Sync function to manually remove the directory
  - `[Symbol.dispose]()`: Automatic cleanup for `using`

Both functions stash the full path at creation time to handle `process.chdir()` correctly, and recursively remove directory contents on disposal.

## Test plan

Passing all upstream Node.js tests:

✅ `test/js/node/test/parallel/test-fs-promises-mkdtempDisposable.js`  
✅ `test/js/node/test/parallel/test-fs-mkdtempDisposableSync.js`

Tests cover:
- Automatic cleanup with `await using` and `using`
- Manual `remove()` calls (both sync and async)
- Encoding options
- Cleanup of directories with nested contents
- Error handling

Fixes #24499

author: lbds137
body:
## Summary

Replace message-count based context windows with token budgets for accurate LLM context management.

## Problem

Gemini identified that using message counts (e.g., 30 messages) for context windows is fundamentally flawed:
- **Text-only chats**: 30 messages × 500 tokens = 15k tokens (wastes 92% of 200k context window)
- **Multimedia chats**: 1 heavy message (voice + images + refs) = 16k tokens, so 30 messages = 480k tokens (exceeds model limits)

## Solution

Implement token-based context budgets that adapt to message content:
- System prompt + current message + memories + history = total context window
- History budget scales dynamically: `contextWindow - system - current - memories`
- Works backwards from newest message to fill available tokens

## Changes

### Schema & Database
- ✅ Rename `contextWindowSize` → `contextWindowTokens`
- ✅ Migration with 128k token default (131,072)
- ✅ Update PersonalityService to load new field

### Token Counting Infrastructure
- ✅ Add tiktoken-based token counter utility
- ✅ Accurate text token counting (gpt-4 encoding)
- ✅ Token estimates for images (1000) and audio (32/second)
- ✅ 32 comprehensive tests for token counting

### AI Worker
- ✅ Refactor ConversationalRAGService to use token budgets
- ✅ Calculate dynamic history budget
- ✅ Add detailed token usage logging
- ✅ Add token counting methods to PromptBuilder

### Bot Client
- ✅ Update MessageHandler to retrieve 100 messages
- ✅ Let AI worker trim based on token budget

## Testing

- ✅ All 753 tests passing
- ✅ TypeScript builds successful
- ✅ Pre-commit hooks pass

## Next Steps

After merge, will need to:
1. Update database LLM configs with appropriate token values (128k for most models, 256k for Gemini)
2. Test with real conversations to verify token budgets

## Breaking Changes

None - migration preserves existing configs with sensible defaults.

author: copilot
body:
Archetypal patterns contained template structures with placeholders but lacked the full domain-specific implementations available in UIA source files.

## Changes

### Content Integration
- Extract Physical/Social/Conceptual/Psychic domain implementations from 253 UIA markdown files
- Add `domain_specific_content` field to all patterns in `archetypal_patterns.json`
- Coverage: 253 Physical (100%), 67 Social/Conceptual/Psychic (26.5% each, matching UIA source availability)

### Schema & Validation
- Update `archetypal_pattern_schema.json` with `domain_specific_content` object definition
- Add `validate_domain_content.py` for content quality checks
- Update test suite to validate 253 patterns vs previous 102

### Documentation
- Document new field structure and usage patterns in `ARCHETYPAL_SCHEMA_README.md`
- Add domain content demo in `demo_archetypal_schema.py`

## Usage

Patterns now provide both template transformation and authoritative UIA content:

```python
pattern = data['patterns'][0]  # Independent domains

# Template approach (customizable)
archetypal = pattern['archetypal_pattern']
# "Balance between {{domains}} will not be achieved unless..."

# Full UIA content (detailed)
physical = pattern['domain_specific_content']['physical']
# "Metropolitan regions will not come to balance until each one is 
#  small and autonomous enough to be an independent sphere of influence.
#  Whenever possible, evolution of such regions should be encouraged..."
```

All tests pass (7/7), zero security alerts, backward compatible.

author: ghost
body:
## Summary

  This pull request introduces the initial project setup and foundationl
  structure for the EasyParking system. It establishes a monorepo
  architecture using pnpm workspaces and integrates Turborepo for
  efficient build and task management.

  ## Key Changes

   * pnpm Workspace: A pnpm-workspace.yaml file has been added to define
     the monorepo structure. This will manage the different parts of the
     application, including:
       * app/*: For individual applications (e.g., frontend, backend).
       * packages/*: For shared libraries and components.
       * e2e: For end-to-end tests.

   * Turborepo Integration: A turbo.json file has been configured to
     manage the build process across the monorepo. This will optimize
     build times and streamline development workflows by defining tasks
     such as build, lint, test, and dev.

   * Dependency Installation: Numerous dependencies have been added to
     the pnpm-lock.yaml file, providing the necessary packages for the
     new project structure and to support future development.

  This foundational work paves the way for modular development,
  improved build performance, and a scalable architecture.

author: sasonaldekant
body:
## fix(design-tokens): Register transformGroup 'dyn/css' globally for Style Dictionary v4 compatibility

This PR fixes the remaining Style Dictionary v4 error for unknown transformGroup "dyn/css" when building design tokens in ESM mode. The custom transformGroup is now registered on the global StyleDictionary object (not per-instance) which aligns with Style Dictionary v4 ESM usage. This resolves the platform config error and allows fully functional ESM token builds, completing the spec requirements.

**Changes:**
- Moved registration of custom transforms and transform groups in `config.js` to the global StyleDictionary object.
- No changes required in `transforms.js` or build runner.
- Fully ESM-compliant and compatible with Node.js 20 and dynui-fixed-enhanced-specification.md.

**How to test:**
- Clean and build design tokens as before: `pnpm --filter @dynui-max/design-tokens build`
- Build completes successfully, all targets produced.

---

Closes ESM module & transformGroup registration issue for project.

#### What is the purpose of this change?

It appears to me that the `If-None-Match` and `If-Match` conditional request headers aren’t supported by rclone with S3.

`2025/11/07 15:26:02 ERROR : protected-new-new.txt: Don't know how to set key "If-None-Match" on upload`

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/conditional-writes.html

#### Was the change discussed in an issue or in the forum before?

https://forum.rclone.org/t/does-rclone-s3-support-if-none-match-and-if-match-upload-headers/52961/13

body:
## 概要
タイムスタンプ正規化画面において、楽曲表示を2行形式から1行形式（楽曲名 / アーティスト名）に統一しました。

## 現状の問題
以下の3箇所で楽曲情報が2行表示されていました:
- Spotify検索結果
- 楽曲マスタ一覧
- Spotify選択楽曲情報

```
楽曲名（1行目）
アーティスト名（2行目、グレー文字）
```

## 変更内容

### 1. Spotify検索結果 (`resources/js/songs/normalize.js:492-508`)
2行表示を1行にまとめ、「楽曲名 / アーティスト名」形式に変更

**修正前**:
```javascript
const title = document.createElement('div');
title.className = 'font-medium text-sm';
title.textContent = track.name;

const artist = document.createElement('div');
artist.className = 'text-xs text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400';
artist.textContent = track.artists.map(a => a.name).join(', ');
```

**修正後**:
```javascript
const songInfo = document.createElement('div');
songInfo.className = 'text-sm truncate';

const titleSpan = document.createElement('span');
titleSpan.className = 'font-medium';
titleSpan.textContent = track.name;

const artistNames = track.artists.map(a => a.name).join(', ');
const separatorSpan = document.createElement('span');
separatorSpan.className = 'text-gray-500 dark:text-gray-400';
separatorSpan.textContent = ' / ' + artistNames;

songInfo.appendChild(titleSpan);
songInfo.appendChild(separatorSpan);
songInfo.title = `${track.name} / ${artistNames}`;
```

### 2. 楽曲マスタ一覧 (`resources/js/songs/normalize.js:793-808`)
Spotify検索結果と同様の1行形式に変更

### 3. Spotify選択楽曲情報
- **HTML構造変更** (`resources/views/songs/index.blade.php:103-106`)
  - 2つのdiv要素（title/artist）を1つに統合
- **JavaScript更新処理変更** (`resources/js/songs/normalize.js:438-459`)
  - DOM操作で1行形式を動的生成

## 実装の特徴

### UI/UX
- **`truncate`クラス**: 長い楽曲名を自動省略
- **`title`属性**: ホバー時に全文表示
- **スタイル**: 楽曲名は太字、アーティスト名はグレー文字

### セキュリティ
- DOM操作による自動エスケープでXSS対策済み
- `innerHTML`は使用せず、`textContent`と`appendChild`を使用

## 期待される効果
- ✅ **縦スペース削減**: 各楽曲アイテムが2行→1行になり、表示効率が約50%向上
- ✅ **一覧性向上**: スクロールなしでより多くの楽曲を一度に確認可能
- ✅ **統一感**: タイムスタンプステータス表示と形式が統一される
- ✅ **可読性**: 「楽曲名 / アーティスト名」の形式は一般的で理解しやすい

## 表示例
```
Let It Be / The Beatles
Bohemian Rhapsody / Queen
Hotel California / Eagles
```

Fixes #108

The optimized code achieves a **140% speedup** by replacing an inefficient list operation with a more performant approach. The key optimization is changing `stack.insert(0, v)` to `stack.append(v)` followed by a single `stack.reverse()` call.

**What changed:**

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **4.3.4** to **7.11.1**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.11.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: if the measurement core defaults to "sysmon" (the default for Python
  3.14+ since v7.9.1), but sysmon can't support some aspect of your
  configuration (concurrency settings, dynamic contexts, and so on), then the
  ctrace core is used instead. Previously, this would result in an error.
  Now a warning is issued instead, explaining the fallback. An explicit request
  for sysmon with conflicting settings will still result in an error. Closes
  `issue 2064`_.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

.. _issue 1420: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1420
.. _issue 2064: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2064
.. _issue 2070: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2070


.. _changes_7-11-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.9, declared support for Python 3.15 alpha.


.. _changes_7-10-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.7
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Performance: with branch coverage in large files, generating HTML, JSON, or
  LCOV reports could take far too long due to some quadratic behavior when
  creating the function and class index pages.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 2048`_.  Thanks to Daniel Diniz for help diagnosing the problem.

- Most warnings and a few errors now have links to a page in the docs
  explaining the specific message.  Closes `issue 1921`_.

.. _issue 1921: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1921
.. _issue 2048: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2048


.. _changes_7-10-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.6
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: ``source`` directories were not properly communicated to subprocesses
  that ran in different directories, as reported in `issue 1499`_.  This is now
  fixed.

- Performance: `Alex Gaynor continues fine-tuning <pull 2038_>`_ the speed of
  combination, especially with many contexts.

.. _issue 1499: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1499
.. _pull 2038: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2038


.. _changes_7-10-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.5
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Big speed improvements for ``coverage combine``: it's now about twice as
  fast! Huge thanks to Alex Gaynor for pull requests `2032 <pull 2032_>`_,
  `2033 <pull 2033_>`_, and `2034 <pull 2034_>`_.

.. _pull 2032: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2032
.. _pull 2033: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2033
.. _pull 2034: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2034


.. _changes_7-10-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.4
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Added ``patch = fork`` for times when the built-in forking support is
  insufficient.

- Fix: ``patch = execv`` also inherits the entire coverage configuration now.


.. _changes_7-10-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fixes for ``patch = subprocess``:

  - If subprocesses spawned yet more subprocesses simultaneously, some coverage
    could be missed.  This is now fixed, closing `issue 2024`_.

  - If subprocesses were created in other directories, their data files were
    stranded there and not combined into the totals, as described in `issue
    2025`_.  This is now fixed.

  - On Windows (or maybe only some Windows?) the patch would fail with a
    ``ModuleNotFound`` error trying to import coverage.  This is now fixed,
    closing `issue 2022`_.

  - Originally only options set in the coverage configuration file would apply
    to subprocesses.  Options set on the ``coverage run`` command line (such as
    ``--branch``) wouldn't be communicated to the subprocesses.  This could
    lead to combining failures, as described in `issue 2021`_. Now the entire
    configuration is used in subprocesses, regardless of its origin.

  - Added ``debug=patch`` to help diagnose problems.

- Fix: really close all SQLite databases, even in-memory ones. Closes `issue
  2017`_.

.. _issue 2017: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2017
.. _issue 2021: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2021
.. _issue 2022: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2022
.. _issue 2024: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2024
.. _issue 2025: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2025


.. _changes_7-10-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some code with NOP bytecodes could report missing branches that are
  actually executed. This is now fixed, closing `issue 1999`_. Python 3.9
  still shows the problem.

.. _issue 1999: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1999


.. _changes_7-10-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the exclusion for ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` was wrong: it marked the branch
  as partial, but it should have been a line exclusion so the entire clause
  would be excluded. Improves `issue 831`_.

- Fix: changed where .pth files are written for ``patch = subprocess``, closing
  `issue 2006`_.

.. _issue 2006: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2006


.. _changes_7-10-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- A new configuration option: ":ref:`config_run_patch`" specifies named patches
  to work around some limitations in coverage measurement.  These patches are
  available:

  - ``patch = _exit`` lets coverage save its data even when :func:`os._exit()
    <python:os._exit>` is used to abruptly end the process.  This closes
    long-standing `issue 310`_ as well as its duplicates: `issue 312`_, `issue
    1673`_, `issue 1845`_, and `issue 1941`_.

  - ``patch = subprocess`` measures coverage in Python subprocesses created
    with :mod:`subprocess`, :func:`os.system`, or one of the :func:`execv
    <python:os.execl>` or :func:`spawnv <python:os.spawnl>` family of
    functions. Closes old `issue 367`_, its duplicate `issue 378`_ and old
    `issue 689`_.

  - ``patch = execv`` adjusts the :func:`execv <python:os.execl>` family of
    functions to save coverage data before ending the current program and
    starting the next. Not available on Windows. Closes `issue 43`_ after 15
    years!

- The HTML report now dimly colors subsequent lines in multi-line statements.
  They used to have no color.  This gives a better indication of the amount of
  code missing in the report.  Closes `issue 1308`_.

- Two new exclusion patterns are part of the defaults: ``...`` is automatically
  excluded as a line and ``if TYPE_CHECKING:`` is excluded as a branch.  Closes
  `issue 831`_.

- A new command-line option: ``--save-signal=USR1`` specifies a signal that
  coverage.py will listen for.  When the signal is sent, the coverage data will
  be saved.  This makes it possible to save data from within long-running
  processes.  Thanks, `Arkady Gilinsky <pull 1
